articles.summary: We report a scanning photoemission spectromicroscopy (SPEM) study on BaFe 2 Se 3 which belongs to the family of two-leg ladder Fe chalcogenides. Although BaFe 2 Se 3 is expected to be a Mott insulator with high spin state of Fe 2+ ions, the itinerant Fe 3d electrons are observed near the Fermi level, coexisting with the localized ones. The SPEM measurement with submicron space resolution shows that the itinerant and localized states spatially coexist, excluding phase separation with the micrometer scale. The localized e g spectral features significantly depend on the wave vector along the rung direction, indicating significant inter-ladder hybridization.
